At compile time, checked word for word by the message tests of `test/messages` with clang:

[cols="2,1,7",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Checked on |The message, and its fix

|`+aead_not_a_family+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: ciphers::aead takes an AEAD family: families::chacha20_poly1305, families::chacha20_poly1305_original, families::xchacha20_poly1305, families::secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305 or families::secretbox_xchacha20poly1305.+`

The fix: Name one of the three ChaCha20-Poly1305 families or the two secret boxes'; AES-GCM is `+ciphers::gcm+`, as in `+aes256_gcm+`.

|`+aes_on_bearssl+`
|native, wasip2
|`+webcpp::crypto: ciphers::aes256<backends::bearssl>: BearSSL exports AES only inside its modes, with no block cipher. Name a backend that exports it, as in ciphers::aes256<backends::ctaes> or ciphers::aes256<backends::openssl>, and add its library to the program's Jamfile.+`

The fix: Name `+ciphers::aes256<backends::ctaes>+`, include `+<webcpp/crypto/backends/ctaes.hpp>+` and add `+/third_party//ctaes+`.

|`+bearssl_not_linked+`
|native, wasip2
|`+webcpp::crypto: the backend BearSSL is used and not linked. In the program's Jamfile, add /third_party//bearssl beside /webcpp/crypto//crypto. (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_BEARSSL=1 and link BearSSL built with webcpp's src/canary_bearssl.c)+`

The fix: Add `+/third_party//bearssl+`.

|`+box_default_not_linked+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: X25519-XSalsa20-Poly1305 sealed box's default backend on this target is libsodium, which is not linked, and the one backend that has it there. Add /webcpp/crypto//sealed_box-default, the default's library on every target, to the program's Jamfile, as in: exe app : app.cpp /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//sealed_box-default ; (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_SODIUM=1 and link libsodium built with webcpp's src/canary_sodium.c)+`

The fix: The secret boxes', the boxes' and the sealed boxes' default is libsodium on every target: add the family's alias, as `+/webcpp/crypto//box_xsalsa20poly1305-default+`, which links `+/third_party//sodium+`.

|`+box_not_a_family+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: hybrid::basic_box takes a box family: families::box_xsalsa20poly1305 or families::box_xchacha20poly1305.+`

The fix: Name `+families::box_xsalsa20poly1305+` or `+families::box_xchacha20poly1305+`, or use `+hybrid::box+` or `+hybrid::box_xchacha20poly1305+`.

|`+chacha_default_not_linked+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: XChaCha20-Poly1305's default backend on this target is libsodium, which is not linked, and the one backend that has it there. Add /webcpp/crypto//xchacha20_poly1305-default, the default's library on every target, to the program's Jamfile, as in: exe app : app.cpp /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//xchacha20_poly1305-default ; (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_SODIUM=1 and link libsodium built with webcpp's src/canary_sodium.c)+`

The fix: The ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEADs' default is libsodium on every target: add the family's alias, as `+/webcpp/crypto//chacha20_poly1305-default+`, which links `+/third_party//sodium+`.

|`+chacha_header_not_included+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: bearssl's ChaCha20-Poly1305 is in <webcpp/crypto/backends/bearssl.hpp>, which the program does not include. Include it, and add /third_party//bearssl to the program's Jamfile.+`

The fix: Include the backend's header the message names, as `+<webcpp/crypto/backends/bearssl.hpp>+`, and add its library, as `+/third_party//bearssl+`.

|`+chacha_on_ctaes+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: ctaes has no ChaCha20-Poly1305. The backends that have it: sodium (native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten), bearssl (native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten), openssl (native, wasip2, wasip3).+`

The fix: Name a backend that has ChaCha20-Poly1305, as in `+chacha20_poly1305<backends::bearssl>+`, or its default, `+chacha20_poly1305<>+`, and link its library.

|`+chacha_unknown_backend+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: ChaCha20-Poly1305 has no backend of that name. The backends that have it: sodium (native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten), bearssl (native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten), openssl (native, wasip2, wasip3).+`

The fix: Name a backend of `+webcpp::crypto::backends+` that has the family, as `+backends::bearssl+`, or leave the backend out for the family's default: `+chacha20_poly1305<>+`.

|`+ctaes_not_linked+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: the backend ctaes is used and not linked. In the program's Jamfile, add /third_party//ctaes beside /webcpp/crypto//crypto. (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_CTAES=1 and link ctaes.c with webcpp's src/canary_ctaes.c)+`

The fix: Add `+/third_party//ctaes+`.

|`+default_openssl_wasm+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_OPENSSL no longer chooses a default. Write the backend in the type where the program wants it, as in ciphers::gcm<ciphers::aes256<backends::openssl>>.+`

The fix: Remove the define, and name `+gcm<aes256<backends::openssl>>+` where the program wants OpenSSL.

|`+default_selected+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_BEARSSL no longer chooses a default. Write the backend in the type where the program wants it, as in ciphers::gcm<ciphers::aes256<backends::bearssl>>.+`

The fix: Remove the define, and name `+gcm<aes256<backends::bearssl>>+` where the program wants BearSSL.

|`+ed25519_default_not_linked+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: Ed25519's default backend on this target is libsodium, which is not linked, and the one backend that has it there. Add /webcpp/crypto//ed25519-default, the default's library on every target, to the program's Jamfile, as in: exe app : app.cpp /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//ed25519-default ; (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_SODIUM=1 and link libsodium built with webcpp's src/canary_sodium.c)+`

The fix: Add `+/webcpp/crypto//ed25519-default+`, which links `+/third_party//sodium+` on every target.

|`+ed25519_on_bearssl+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: bearssl has no Ed25519. The backends that have it: sodium (native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten).+`

The fix: Leave the backend out, as in `+curves::ed25519::keypair+`, or name `+backends::sodium+`, and add `+/third_party//sodium+`.

|`+ed25519_unknown_policy+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: Ed25519's only verification policy is curves::ed25519::strict.+`

The fix: Leave the policy out, as in `+curves::ed25519::verify(public_key, message, signature)+`, or name `+curves::ed25519::strict+`.

|`+ed25519ph_sha256+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: Ed25519ph is defined over SHA-512 (RFC 8032 section 5.1); name curves::ed25519::ph<webcpp::hash::sha2_512>.+`

The fix: Name `+curves::ed25519::ph<webcpp::hash::sha2_512>+`: RFC 8032 defines Ed25519ph over SHA-512.

|`+ellswift_other_backend+`
|native, wasip2
|`+webcpp::crypto: bearssl has no ElligatorSwift. The backends that have it: secp256k1 (native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten).+`

The fix: Name `+backends::secp256k1+`, or leave the backend out: `+curves::secp256k1::ellswift_decode(encoded_key)+`.

|`+gcm_default_openssl_not_linked+`
|native
|`+webcpp::crypto: AES-GCM's default backend on this target is OpenSSL, which is not linked. Add /webcpp/crypto//gcm-default, the default's library on every target, to the program's Jamfile, as in: exe app : app.cpp /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//gcm-default ; or name another backend in the type, as in ciphers::gcm<ciphers::aes256<backends::bearssl>>. The backends that have it: bearssl (native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten), openssl (native, wasip2, wasip3). (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_OPENSSL=1 and link libcrypto)+`

The fix: Natively the default is OpenSSL: add `+/webcpp/crypto//gcm-default+`, which links `+/webcpp/crypto//openssl+` there, or name BearSSL in the type, as in `+gcm<aes256<backends::bearssl>>+`.

|`+gcm_on_ctaes+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: ciphers::gcm<ciphers::aes256<backends::ctaes>>: ctaes exports the AES block cipher alone, and webcpp builds no GCM on another library's AES. Use a backend that exports GCM: ciphers::gcm<ciphers::aes256<backends::bearssl>> or ciphers::gcm<ciphers::aes256<backends::openssl>>.+`

The fix: Name `+gcm<aes256<backends::bearssl>>+` or `+gcm<aes256<backends::openssl>>+`, or use `+aes256_gcm+` with its default linked.

|`+heavy_without_threads+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: async_slow runs on another thread and needs a build with threads (natively without WEBCPP_CRYPTO_NO_THREADS; on Emscripten -pthread). Without threads, call slow.+`

The fix: Call the synchronous operation the message names, or build with threads: natively without `+WEBCPP_CRYPTO_NO_THREADS+`, on Emscripten with `+-pthread+`; WASI has none.

|`+heavy_without_threads_first+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: async_slow runs on another thread and needs a build with threads (natively without WEBCPP_CRYPTO_NO_THREADS; on Emscripten -pthread). Without threads, call slow.+`

The fix: As `+heavy_without_threads+`.

|`+kx_default_not_linked+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: crypto_kx's default backend on this target is libsodium, which is not linked, and the one backend that has it there. Add /webcpp/crypto//kx-default, the default's library on every target, to the program's Jamfile, as in: exe app : app.cpp /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//kx-default ; (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_SODIUM=1 and link libsodium built with webcpp's src/canary_sodium.c)+`

The fix: Add `+/webcpp/crypto//kx-default+`, which links `+/third_party//sodium+` on every target.

|`+label_lookup_by_value+`
|native, wasip2
|`+no matching function for call to 'scan_outputs'+`

The fix: Return `+std::optional<std::span<std::uint8_t const, 32>>+`, a span over a tweak the lookup keeps, such as a map's entry; never the tweak by value.

|`+musig_nonce_copied+`
|native, wasip2
|`+call to deleted constructor of+`

The fix: Pass the nonce with std::move, once: a secret nonce signs one message.

|`+musig_other_backend+`
|native, wasip2
|`+webcpp::crypto: bearssl has no MuSig2. The backends that have it: secp256k1 (native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten).+`

The fix: Name `+backends::secp256k1+`, or leave the backend out: `+curves::secp256k1::musig::parse_public_nonce(encoded_nonce)+`.

|`+no_backend_wasm+`
|wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: AES-GCM's default backend on this target is BearSSL, which is not linked. Add /webcpp/crypto//gcm-default, the default's library on every target, to the program's Jamfile, as in: exe app : app.cpp /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//gcm-default ; or name another backend in the type, as in ciphers::gcm<ciphers::aes256<backends::openssl>>. The backends that have it: bearssl (native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten), openssl (native, wasip2, wasip3). (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_BEARSSL=1 and link BearSSL built with webcpp's src/canary_bearssl.c)+`

The fix: On WASI the default is BearSSL: add `+/webcpp/crypto//gcm-default+`, which links `+/third_party//bearssl+` there, or, with OpenSSL linked, name it in the type, as in `+gcm<aes256<backends::openssl>>+`.

|`+openssl_memory_not_linked+`
|native
|`+webcpp::crypto: WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE routes OpenSSL's allocations, and OpenSSL is not linked. In the program's Jamfile, add /webcpp/crypto//openssl beside /webcpp/crypto//crypto, or remove that define. (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_OPENSSL=1 and link libcrypto)+`

The fix: A target has the define and not OpenSSL: put `+<library>/webcpp/crypto//openssl+` in the same project requirements as the define, or remove the define.

|`+openssl_memory_on_webassembly+`
|wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE is an option of native programs, and this program is built for WebAssembly. Remove that define from the program's Jamfile.+`

The fix: Remove `+<define>WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE+` from the WebAssembly build: give that build a project of its own, without the define and OpenSSL, naming `+/third_party//bearssl+`. On WebAssembly the backend is BearSSL, which allocates nothing.

|`+openssl_not_linked+`
|native, wasip2
|`+webcpp::crypto: the backend OpenSSL is used and not linked. In the program's Jamfile, add /webcpp/crypto//openssl beside /webcpp/crypto//crypto. (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_OPENSSL=1 and link libcrypto)+`

The fix: Add `+/webcpp/crypto//openssl+`.

`+openssl_on_emscripten+`:: `+/webcpp/crypto//openssl+` named in a build for Emscripten. The fix: Name `+/third_party//bearssl+` in its place for the Emscripten build.
+
Its Jamfile:

On each target, the build's output contains:
+
* emscripten:
** `+webcpp::crypto: /webcpp/crypto//openssl is named in a build for Emscripten, where webcpp does not build OpenSSL.+`

`+p256_default_not_linked_on_emscripten+`:: A program for Emscripten that makes a P-256 key pair on its default, BearSSL, and links none. The fix: As `+p256_default_not_linked+`.
+
Its Jamfile:
+
[listing]
----
include::{webcpp-root}/tools/test/fixtures/crypto_jamfiles/p256_default_not_linked_on_emscripten/Jamfile[tag=jamfile]
----
+
On each target, the build's output contains:
+
* emscripten:
** `+webcpp::crypto: P-256's default backend on this target is BearSSL, which is not linked, and the one backend that has it there. Add /webcpp/crypto//p256-default, the default's library on every target, to the program's Jamfile, as in: exe app : app.cpp /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//p256-default ; (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_BEARSSL=1 and link BearSSL built with webcpp's src/canary_bearssl.c)+`

`+p256_on_sodium_on_emscripten+`:: A program for Emscripten that names libsodium, which has no P-256, in a P-256 key pair's type. The fix: As `+p256_on_sodium+`.

`+pem_default_not_linked_on_emscripten+`:: A program for Emscripten that armours DER as PEM on its default, libsodium, and links none. The fix: As `+pem_default_not_linked+`.

On MSVC, each case of `test/msvc` is proven to stop the build, at compile or at link time; its text is MSVC's own, the same instruction in MSVC's words, and two files compiled with different settings stop the link with LNK2038.

[cols="1,1,4",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Stops |Fix

|`+aead_not_a_family+`
|the compile
|Name one of the three ChaCha20-Poly1305 families or the two secret boxes'; AES-GCM is `+ciphers::gcm+`, as in `+aes256_gcm+`.

|`+aes_on_bearssl+`
|the compile
|Name `+ciphers::aes256<backends::ctaes>+`, include `+<webcpp/crypto/backends/ctaes.hpp>+` and add `+/third_party//ctaes+`.

|`+bearssl_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add `+/third_party//bearssl+`.

|`+box_default_not_linked+`
|the compile
|The secret boxes', the boxes' and the sealed boxes' default is libsodium on every target: add the family's alias, as `+/webcpp/crypto//box_xsalsa20poly1305-default+`, which links `+/third_party//sodium+`.

|`+box_not_a_family+`
|the compile
|Name `+families::box_xsalsa20poly1305+` or `+families::box_xchacha20poly1305+`, or use `+hybrid::box+` or `+hybrid::box_xchacha20poly1305+`.

|`+canary_ctaes_missing+`
|the link
|Link `+/third_party//ctaes+`.

|`+canary_missing+`
|the link
|Link the library through b2, `+/third_party//bearssl+`; built by other means, it must be the pinned commit, with webcpp's `+src/canary_bearssl.c+`.

|`+canary_other_commit+`
|the link
|Build the library at the commit of webcpp's submodule, or link it through b2.

|`+canary_other_configuration+`
|the link
|Build BearSSL in webcpp's configuration (`+getentropy+`), or link it through b2.

|`+canary_secp256k1_missing+`
|the link
|Link `+/third_party//secp256k1+`.

|`+canary_secp256k1_small+`
|the link
|Give the program and the library the same `+<webcpp-secp256k1-tables>+`, or link through b2.

|`+canary_secp256k1_two_files+`
|the link
|Compile every file of the program with the same backend settings.

|`+canary_sodium_other_commit+`
|the link
|Build the library at the commit of webcpp's submodule, or link it through b2.

|`+canary_two_files+`
|the link
|Compile every file of the program with the same backend settings.

|`+chacha_default_not_linked+`
|the compile
|The ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEADs' default is libsodium on every target: add the family's alias, as `+/webcpp/crypto//chacha20_poly1305-default+`, which links `+/third_party//sodium+`.

|`+chacha_header_not_included+`
|the compile
|Include the backend's header the message names, as `+<webcpp/crypto/backends/bearssl.hpp>+`, and add its library, as `+/third_party//bearssl+`.

|`+chacha_on_ctaes+`
|the compile
|Name a backend that has ChaCha20-Poly1305, as in `+chacha20_poly1305<backends::bearssl>+`, or its default, `+chacha20_poly1305<>+`, and link its library.

|`+chacha_unknown_backend+`
|the compile
|Name a backend of `+webcpp::crypto::backends+` that has the family, as `+backends::bearssl+`, or leave the backend out for the family's default: `+chacha20_poly1305<>+`.

|`+ctaes_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add `+/third_party//ctaes+`.

|`+default_openssl_wasm+`
|the compile
|Remove the define, and name `+gcm<aes256<backends::openssl>>+` where the program wants OpenSSL.

|`+default_selected+`
|the compile
|Remove the define, and name `+gcm<aes256<backends::bearssl>>+` where the program wants BearSSL.

|`+ed25519_default_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add `+/webcpp/crypto//ed25519-default+`, which links `+/third_party//sodium+` on every target.

|`+ed25519_on_bearssl+`
|the compile
|Leave the backend out, as in `+curves::ed25519::keypair+`, or name `+backends::sodium+`, and add `+/third_party//sodium+`.

|`+ed25519_unknown_policy+`
|the compile
|Leave the policy out, as in `+curves::ed25519::verify(public_key, message, signature)+`, or name `+curves::ed25519::strict+`.

|`+ed25519ph_sha256+`
|the compile
|Name `+curves::ed25519::ph<webcpp::hash::sha2_512>+`: RFC 8032 defines Ed25519ph over SHA-512.

|`+ellswift_other_backend+`
|the compile
|Name `+backends::secp256k1+`, or leave the backend out: `+curves::secp256k1::ellswift_decode(encoded_key)+`.

|`+gcm_default_openssl_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Natively the default is OpenSSL: add `+/webcpp/crypto//gcm-default+`, which links `+/webcpp/crypto//openssl+` there, or name BearSSL in the type, as in `+gcm<aes256<backends::bearssl>>+`.

|`+gcm_on_ctaes+`
|the compile
|Name `+gcm<aes256<backends::bearssl>>+` or `+gcm<aes256<backends::openssl>>+`, or use `+aes256_gcm+` with its default linked.

|`+heavy_without_threads+`
|the compile
|Call the synchronous operation the message names, or build with threads: natively without `+WEBCPP_CRYPTO_NO_THREADS+`, on Emscripten with `+-pthread+`; WASI has none.

|`+kx_default_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add `+/webcpp/crypto//kx-default+`, which links `+/third_party//sodium+` on every target.

|`+label_lookup_by_value+`
|the compile
|Return `+std::optional<std::span<std::uint8_t const, 32>>+`, a span over a tweak the lookup keeps, such as a map's entry; never the tweak by value.

|`+memory_missing_definition_install+`
|the link
|Define `+std::pmr::memory_resource& webcpp::crypto::openssl_memory_resource() noexcept+` once in the program, returning a resource that is never destroyed.

|`+memory_missing_definition_make+`
|the link
|Define `+std::pmr::memory_resource& webcpp::crypto::openssl_memory_resource() noexcept+` once in the program, returning a resource that is never destroyed.

|`+memory_two_files+`
|the link
|Give the define in the requirements of the program's project, with OpenSSL beside it, `+project app : requirements <define>WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE <library>/webcpp/crypto//openssl ;+`, so that every target of the program gets both.

|`+musig_nonce_copied+`
|the compile
|Pass the nonce with std::move, once: a secret nonce signs one message.

|`+musig_other_backend+`
|the compile
|Name `+backends::secp256k1+`, or leave the backend out: `+curves::secp256k1::musig::parse_public_nonce(encoded_nonce)+`.

|`+openssl_memory_not_linked+`
|the compile
|A target has the define and not OpenSSL: put `+<library>/webcpp/crypto//openssl+` in the same project requirements as the define, or remove the define.

|`+openssl_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add `+/webcpp/crypto//openssl+`.

|`+openssl_old+`
|the compile
|Name `+/webcpp/crypto//openssl+`, which builds OpenSSL 3.5.9; without b2, put OpenSSL 3's `+include/+` first.

|`+p256_default_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add `+/webcpp/crypto//p256-default+`, which links `+/third_party//bearssl+` on every target.

|`+p256_on_sodium+`
|the compile
|Leave the backend out, as in `+curves::p256::keypair+`, or name `+backends::bearssl+`, and add `+/third_party//bearssl+`.

|`+pem_default_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add `+/webcpp/crypto//pem-default+`, which links `+/third_party//sodium+` on every target.

|`+secp256k1_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add `+/third_party//secp256k1+`.

|`+secp256k1_other_backend+`
|the compile
|Name `+backends::secp256k1+`, or leave the backend out: `+curves::secp256k1::keypair+`.

|`+secret_of_no_bytes+`
|the compile
|Give `+secret+` the number of bytes it holds, at least one, as in `+secret<32>+`.

|`+silent_payments_other_backend+`
|the compile
|Name `+backends::secp256k1+`, or leave the backend out: `+curves::secp256k1::silent_payments::make_prevouts_summary(...)+`.

|`+sodium_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add `+/third_party//sodium+`.

|`+x25519_default_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add `+/webcpp/crypto//x25519-default+`, which links `+/third_party//sodium+` on every target.
|===

Elsewhere than MSVC these mistakes build, and nothing stops them; the fixtures record it:
